A recursively self-upgrading agentic harness you can modify and remix. It launches any coding agent with Hanzo’s tools attached, routes model calls through Hanzo, and links the session to your account.
The coding agent Hanzo builds, with Kai deciding each step. It is the agent Gen opens when none is named.
The agent you use is a flag.
Each launches as itself, with its own interface and its own habits, and Gen around it. gen --help lists every one.
Tools, models, sessions and fences, each set by a flag.
The Hanzo MCP toolset rides along on every agent that can take a server for one run.
Its model calls go to api.hanzo.ai, metered on your account, for an agent that can name another endpoint. Without the flag, an agent uses the account it is signed in to.
Signed in, a session is linked to your Hanzo account and streams to mission control as it runs, so it can be followed and picked back up.
Sessions are approved inside a sandbox; ask before each action instead. A repository’s own .mcp.json stays off until you trust it.

The same harness, as hanzo dev.

The harness, every agent's launcher and how its output is read are on GitHub, one file an agent.

curl -fsSL https://hanzo.sh | sh -s gen installs gen alone; curl -fsSL https://hanzo.sh | sh installs every Hanzo tool, gen and the Hanzo CLI included. Run either again to upgrade. On Windows, take the build from the release page.
Is gen the same as hanzo dev?
The same harness. The Hanzo CLI links it, so gen --claude and hanzo dev --claude take the same flags and run the same session. Bare gen, like bare hanzo dev, opens Hanzo Dev.
Does every agent run on Hanzo’s models?
Only when you pass --cloud, and only an agent that can name another endpoint. Without it, each agent keeps the account it is signed in to.
On --cloud, the agent’s model calls, on your Hanzo account. On the agent’s own account, only what Hanzo’s tools handled for it.
No. Each agent runs as itself — its own interface and its own commands — and anything after -- goes to it untouched.
